hint.en: with models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6

description.en: Rules that engineering teams and open-source projects set for work done with agents: how agent-written changes are disclosed and reviewed, who may let an agent act in shared spaces, who owns the shared agent setup, and how hiring interviews change.
description.ru: Правила, которые команды разработки и открытые проекты вводят для работы с агентами: как раскрывать и проверять изменения, написанные агентом, кто может пускать агента в общие пространства, кто владеет общей настройкой агентов и как меняются собеседования.

definition.en: The practice in which one agent does the work and a second agent, often on a different model, reviews it with the task of finding problems. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой один агент выполняет работу, а второй, часто на другой модели, проверяет её с задачей найти проблемы. [1][2][3]

firstAppeared.note: Jesse Vincent, *Agentic slop PRs* (Mar 31 2026) and *My favorite adversarial review prompt* (May 1 2026); concept generalized through the Superpowers plugin.

sources.quote: I typically double-ESC to reset the architect to a previous checkpoint and tell it to review up to the now-current checkpoint.
sources.author: Jesse Vincent

sources.quote: Writer/Reviewer pattern. Session A implements the change. Session B reviews it in a completely fresh context, no prior conversation baggage.
sources.author: Arpan Patel

definition.en: An approach in which the development process works as a black box that turns specifications into software, and people do not write the code. [1]
definition.ru: Подход, при котором процесс разработки работает как чёрный ящик, превращающий спецификации в софт, и люди не пишут код. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Dan Shapiro's six-level framework, popularized via Simon Willison, *The Five Levels: from Spicy Autocomplete to the Dark Factory* (Jan 28 2026).

sources.quote: And your software process isn’t really a software process any more. It’s a black box that turns specs into software.
sources.author: Dan Shapiro

definition.en: The practice in which, after each agent mistake, the developer adds a rule, a script or a check to the agent's environment so that the mistake does not happen again. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой после каждой ошибки агента разработчик добавляет в его окружение правило, скрипт или проверку, чтобы ошибка не повторилась. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Mitchell Hashimoto, *My AI Adoption Journey* (Feb 5 2026).

sources.quote: I've grown to calling this "harness engineering." It is the idea that anytime you find an agent makes a mistake, you take the time to engineer a solution such that the agent never makes that mistake again.
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

sources.quote: Review comments, refactoring pull requests, and user-facing bugs are captured as documentation updates or encoded directly into tooling.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

definition.en: The practice in which project instructions for the agent (commands, conventions, constraints) are kept in a text document that the agent reads at the start of every session. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой инструкции для агента по проекту (команды, соглашения, ограничения) хранят в текстовом документе, который агент читает в начале каждой сессии. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: term stabilized through 2025 alongside CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md adoption.

sources.quote: Think of AGENTS.md as a README for agents: a dedicated, predictable place to provide the context and instructions to help AI coding agents work on your project.
sources.author: agents.md community

sources.quote: Start with Guardrails, Not a Manual. Your CLAUDE.md should start small, documenting based on what Claude is getting wrong.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

definition.en: The practice in which one agent holds the plan, hands subtasks to worker agents and merges their results. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой один агент ведёт план, раздаёт подзадачи агентам-исполнителям и сводит их результаты. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: multi-agent literature; named pattern crystallized through Wilson Lin's planners → sub-planners → workers → judges shape (via Willison Jan 19 2026) and Anthropic Agents SDK examples.

sources.quote: Our Research system uses a multi-agent architecture with an orchestrator-worker pattern, where a lead agent coordinates the process while delegating to specialized subagents that operate in parallel.
sources.author: Anthropic (engineering blog, no personal byline in saved text)

sources.quote: Planners continuously explore the codebase and create tasks. They can spawn sub-planners for specific areas, making planning itself parallel and recursive.
sources.author: Wilson Lin

definition.en: An approach in which a team agrees that people neither write nor review the code: the team states the intent, and evals control the quality. [1][2]
definition.ru: Подход, при котором команда договаривается, что люди не пишут и не ревьюят код: команда формулирует намерение, а качество контролируют эвалы. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Simon Willison, *How StrongDM's AI team build serious software without even looking at the code* (Feb 7 2026).

sources.quote: We built a Software Factory: non-interactive development where specs + scenarios drive agents that write code, run harnesses, and converge without human review.
sources.author: Justin McCarthy

sources.quote: Throughout the development process, humans never directly contributed any code. This became a core philosophy for the team: no manually-written code.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

definition.en: Building software by talking to an agent without reading the code: every change is accepted, errors are pasted back until it works.
definition.ru: Разработка разговором с агентом без чтения кода: все правки принимаются, ошибки вставляются обратно, пока не заработает.

firstAppeared.note: Andrej Karpathy, X/Twitter, Feb 2 2025

sources.quote: There's a new kind of coding I call "vibe coding", where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.
sources.author: Andrej Karpathy

origin.ru: Термин ввёл Андрей Карпаты в посте в X
origin.en: Coined by Andrej Karpathy in a post on X

definition.en: The practice in which the agent first lays out steps, risks and checks, and the developer corrects that outline before any code is written. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент сначала описывает шаги, риски и проверки, а разработчик правит это описание до начала работы над кодом. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: If you want to iterate on the plan, it helps to explicitly include instructions in the prompt to not proceed with implementation until the plan has been accepted by the user.
sources.author: Indragie Karunaratne

sources.quote: Check out the current state of the project in our working directory to understand where we're starting off, then ask me questions, one at a time, to help refine the idea.
sources.author: Jesse Vincent

sources.quote: Tip: Creating a comprehensive plan interactively with an agent is a really important
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

definition.en: The practice in which the developer reworks the agent's implementation by hand after the agent has finished. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик руками дорабатывает реализацию после того, как агент закончил работу. [1][2]

sources.quote: I almost always go in after an AI does work
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

sources.quote: I still edit the code manually to ensure the narrative is clear, to keep my mental model of the problem up to date, and to ensure that the code actually does what it purports to do.
sources.author: Conrad Irwin

title.en: Change of approach after repeated failures

definition.en: The practice in which, after the agent fails at the same problem several times, the developer switches to a different approach. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой после нескольких неудач агента на одной задаче разработчик переходит к другому подходу. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: It's at this point that I know I need to step back, review what it did,
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

sources.quote: Use the /model command to switch to a different model and try again. Switching between GPT-4o and Sonnet will often get past problems.
sources.author: aider.chat

sources.quote: One classic sign that you’ve got a loop spinning in place is the same command being tried over and over without any change in the result. Give the same command a third time with no change from the second and it’s probably time to stop.
sources.author: Addy Osmani

definition.en: The practice in which the developer writes the critical and complex parts of the code and hands the rest to the agent. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик сам пишет критичные и сложные части кода, а остальное отдаёт агенту. [1][2]

sources.quote: Write the critical parts and ask AI to do the rest.
sources.author: Anton Zhiyanov

sources.quote: Engineers tend to delegate tasks that are easily verifiable, where they “can relatively easily sniff-check on correctness”, low-stakes (e.g. “throwaway debug or research code”), or boring (“The more excited I am to do the task, the more likely I am to not use Claude”).
sources.author: Saffron Huang, Bryan Seethor, Esin Durmus, Kunal Handa, Miles McCain, Michael Stern, Deep Ganguli

definition.en: An approach in which the specification is the source of truth: the developer edits the specification, and the agent generates the code from it. [1][2][4]
definition.ru: Подход, при котором источником правды служит спецификация: разработчик правит её, а агент генерирует по ней код. [1][2][4]

sources.quote: main.md is the actual source code of the app: the Markdown instructions file. Whenever I need to add features or fix bugs, I edit this file.
sources.author: GitHub Engineering

sources.quote: We prioritize work, translate user feedback into acceptance criteria, and validate outcomes.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

definition.en: The practice in which the agent's context is cleared before an unrelated task begins. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой контекст агента очищают перед началом не связанной задачи. [1][2]

sources.quote: /clear between unrelated tasks. It costs nothing, and it means the next task doesn’t keep paying for the previous one’s history.
sources.author: Anthropic

sources.quote: Use /clear to discard the chat history and make a fresh start.
sources.author: aider.chat

definition.en: The practice in which the model and its reasoning level are chosen for each task by modality, context length, tool-call reliability, latency and cost. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой модель и уровень рассуждений выбирают под каждую задачу по модальности, длине контекста, надёжности вызова инструментов, задержке и цене. [1]

sources.quote: Sonnet costs 3-4x less than Opus here and works just as well for clicking around.
sources.author: Abhishek Ray

definition.en: The practice in which one instruction document is canonical and the documents of other agent tools point to it through a pointer line, a symlink or an include. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой один документ с инструкциями считается основным, а документы других инструментов ссылаются на него строкой-указателем, симлинком или включением. [1][2]

sources.quote: CLAUDE.md supports @path imports, and those do not depend on the flag.
sources.author: Przemek

sources.quote: Symlink all three and every agent reads the same file.
sources.author: FerroxLabs

definition.en: The practice in which the developer stops the agent as soon as it goes in a wrong direction and gives it a correction. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик останавливает агента, как только тот уходит не туда, и даёт поправку. [1][2]

sources.quote: Watch the first minute, press Esc the moment Claude drifts, and after two failed corrections run /clear and write a better prompt instead of a third.
sources.author: Anthropic

sources.quote: Watch for signs the agent is off-track: unexpected file changes, repetitive attempts at the same fix, or TODO comments where real code should be. When you see these, stop and try to understand why the agent ran aground.
sources.author: Mikayla Maki

definition.en: The practice in which the developer explains a problem to the agent, gets its feedback and works out the solution together with it. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик объясняет агенту задачу, получает его замечания и вырабатывает решение вместе с ним. [1]

sources.quote: Occasionally it feels like magic, but nowadays with Claude Code, it feels like pairing with someone with a few years under their belt who just needs the occasional nudge.
sources.author: Orta Therox

definition.en: The practice in which the developer uses an agent to learn a language or a concept and then writes the code without it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик с помощью агента изучает язык или концепцию, а код затем пишет сам. [1][2]

sources.quote: I’m leveraging them to learn Go, to upskill myself. And then I apply this new knowledge when I code.
sources.author: Alberto Fortin

sources.quote: When onboarding to a new codebase, use the agent for learning and exploration.
sources.author: Lee Robinson

definition.en: The practice in which the tools an agent calls are made to respond quickly, report errors clearly and withstand misuse. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой инструменты, которые вызывает агент, делают быстрыми, с понятными сообщениями об ошибках и устойчивыми к неправильному использованию. [1][2]

sources.quote: Tools need to be fast. The quicker they respond (and the less
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

sources.quote: That’s patching a human problem. Instead, write a simple bash wrapper with a clear, intuitive API and document that.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

definition.en: The practice in which several agents work on separate tasks at the same time, each in its own isolated copy of the repository. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько агентов одновременно работают над разными задачами, каждый в своей изолированной копии репозитория. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: By default sketch creates a little development environment in a container with a copy of the source code and the runner has the ability to extract git commits from the container. This lets you run many simultaneously.
sources.author: David Crawshaw

sources.quote: Work on a feature in one terminal while Claude fixes a bug in another, without the edits colliding.
sources.author: Anthropic

definition.en: The practice in which permission prompts are switched off for tasks whose changes the developer would accept anyway. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой запросы подтверждений отключают для задач, чьи правки разработчик принял бы в любом случае. [1][2]

sources.quote: I disable all permission checks. Which basically means I run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions.
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

sources.quote: Once you have this set up, you can run claude --dangerously-skip-permissions inside the container without worrying about Claude accidentally deleting important files or breaking your system configuration.
sources.author: Jökull Sólberg

definition.en: The practice in which the agent works on a task while the developer is busy with something else. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент работает над задачей, пока разработчик занят другим делом. [1][2]

sources.quote: I think the faster/slower argument for me personally is missing the thing I like the most: the AI can work for me while I step away to do other things.
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

sources.quote: The loop is: kick off a task, pocket the phone, get notified when Claude needs input. Async development from anywhere.
sources.author: Granda

definition.ru: Практика, при которой каждая фича или задача ведётся в отдельной сессии агента, чтобы контекст не разрастался. [1][2]
definition.en: The practice of keeping each feature or task in its own agent session so the context does not bloat. [1][2]

sources.quote: Keep the context short. This means starting a new session per feature.
sources.author: Fabien Sanglard

sources.quote: If you notice the effectiveness of the agent decreasing, it's time to start a new conversation.
sources.author: Lee Robinson

definition.en: A prompting habit in which the model is asked for pros and cons, alternatives and missing points, instead of being asked to confirm an opinion. [1]
definition.ru: Приём, при котором модель просят назвать плюсы и минусы, альтернативы и упущенное, вместо просьбы подтвердить мнение. [1]

sources.quote: My best current technique for avoiding this is a bit of role-play that gives the coding agent a reason not to blindly trust the code review.
sources.author: Jesse Vincent

definition.en: The practice in which work starts on a faster and cheaper model and moves to a more capable one when the task turns out to be hard. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой работу начинают на быстрой и дешёвой модели и переходят на более сильную, когда задача оказывается сложной. [1]

sources.quote: Opus does well when Sonnet gets stuck - start a new window and spam Opus.
sources.author: Sankalp

definition.en: The practice in which the developer picks established libraries that existed before the model's training cutoff. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой выбирают устоявшиеся библиотеки, существовавшие до даты, на которой заканчиваются обучающие данные модели. [1]

sources.quote: I gain enough value from LLMs that I now deliberately consider this when picking a library—I try to stick with libraries with good stability and that are popular enough that many examples of them will have made it into the training data.
sources.author: Simon Willison

definition.en: A prompting habit in which the model is asked for several approaches with the pros and cons of each. [1]
definition.ru: Приём, при котором модель просят предложить несколько подходов с плюсами и минусами каждого. [1]

sources.quote: I’ll use prompts like “what are options for HTTP libraries in Rust?
sources.author: Simon Willison

definition.en: The practice in which the developer drafts the solution without an agent and then gives it to an agent to review and improve. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик сначала набрасывает решение без агента, а затем отдаёт агенту на проверку и улучшение. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: I'm subconsciously defaulting to AI for all things coding.
sources.author: Alberto Fortin

sources.quote: Write the initial version yourself and ask AI to review and improve it.
sources.author: Anton Zhiyanov

sources.quote: Absolutely not. I began by coming up with a rough plan of how I wanted this to work.
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

definition.en: The practice in which a project starts with a quickly generated prototype that shows whether the key requirement can be met. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект начинают с быстро сгенерированного прототипа, показывающего, выполнимо ли ключевое требование. [1]

sources.quote: The best way to start any project is with a prototype that proves that the key requirements of that project can be met.
sources.author: Simon Willison

definition.en: The practice in which the agent is given a screenshot of the result or of a mock-up, and the change and the screenshot are repeated until they match. [1][2][3][4]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенту дают скриншот результата или макета и повторяют правку и скриншот, пока они не совпадут. [1][2][3][4]

sources.quote: Instead, I opened a second copy of Sketch and pasted in a screenshot of the form and wrote “this is ugly, please make it less ugly.

sources.quote: Once a component is working, I give feedback based on screenshots rather than reading through the code. The official best practices guide covers this pattern too: compare a screenshot against the target design and iterate from there.
sources.author: kent-tokyo (DEV Community handle)

definition.en: A prompting habit in which the agent is asked to make an interface “more beautiful” or “more elegant”, with no further detail. [1]
definition.ru: Приём, при котором агента просят сделать интерфейс «красивее» или «элегантнее» без уточнений. [1]

sources.quote: If Claude doesn't produce a well-designed UI the first time, you can just tell it to "make it more beautiful/elegant/usable".
sources.author: Indragie Karunaratne

definition.en: The practice in which systematic and time-consuming tasks, from renames to large migrations, are handed to the agent. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенту отдают систематические и долгие задачи: от переименований до больших миграций. [1][2]

sources.quote: I’m still using LLMs, but for dumber things: "rename all occurrences of this parameter", or "here’s some pseudo code, give me the Go equivalent".
sources.author: Alberto Fortin

sources.quote: Thus, AI's best use case for me remains writing one-off scripts.
sources.author: Colton

definition.en: The practice in which code is kept plain: descriptive function names, no inheritance, no clever constructs. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой код держат простым: говорящие имена функций, без наследования и без хитрых конструкций. [1]

sources.quote: Simple code significantly outperforms complex code in agentic contexts.
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

definition.en: The practice in which a session starts by placing existing code into the context, and changes are made from there. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой сессию начинают с загрузки существующего кода в контекст и дальше вносят изменения от него. [1][2]

sources.quote: I often start a new chat by dumping in existing code to seed that context, then work with the LLM to modify it in some way.
sources.author: Simon Willison

sources.quote: They write specific prompts. The agent's success rate improves significantly with specific instructions.
sources.author: Lee Robinson

definition.en: The practice in which the developer gives function signatures, an outline or scaffolding, and the agent fills in the implementation. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик задаёт сигнатуры функций, каркас или заготовку, а агент пишет реализацию. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: I find LLMs respond extremely well to function signatures like the one I use here.

sources.quote: Write an outline of the code and ask AI to fill the missing parts.

sources.quote: Tip: AI is very good at fill-in-the-blank or draw-the-rest-of-the-owl.

definition.en: The practice in which the agent is given current documentation and examples for a library that is missing from the model's training data. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенту дают актуальную документацию и примеры по библиотеке, которой нет в обучающих данных модели. [1][2]

sources.quote: LLMs can still help you work with libraries that exist outside their training data, but you need to put in more work—you’ll need to feed them recent examples of how those libraries should be used as part of your prompt.

sources.quote: What if we removed the decision entirely? Instead of hoping agents would invoke a skill, we could embed a docs index directly in AGENTS.md.

title.en: Generated code in place of dependencies

definition.en: The practice in which the agent writes the needed code in the project, and a new library is not added. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой нужный код агент пишет в проекте, а новую библиотеку не подключают. [1][2]

sources.quote: Be even more conservative about upgrades than
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

sources.quote: We favored dependencies and abstractions that could be fully internalized and reasoned about in-repo.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

definition.en: The practice in which a system is built with detailed logging, so that an agent can read the logs and find the cause of a problem. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой систему делают с подробным логированием, чтобы агент мог прочитать логи и найти причину проблемы. [1]

sources.quote: In general logging is super important. For instance my app currently has
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

definition.en: The practice in which the agent is given a check it can run (tests, a build, a linter) and repeats the change and the check until the check passes. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенту дают проверку, которую он может запустить (тесты, сборку, линтер), и он повторяет правку и проверку, пока проверка не пройдёт. [1][2]

sources.quote: Claude is most useful when it's capable of independently driving feedback loops that allow it to make a change, test the change, and gather context on what failed to try another iteration.

sources.quote: Warnings are a great example. Is your test suite spitting out a warning that something you are using is deprecated?

definition.en: The practice in which the agent starts subagents to verify details or to investigate separate questions. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент запускает субагентов, чтобы проверить детали или разобрать отдельные вопросы. [1]

sources.quote: By someone who didn’t write the code: in the terminal, /code-review reviews the diff in a fresh subagent that never saw your conversation. It isn’t swayed by the reasoning that produced the code.
sources.author: Anthropic

definition.en: The practice in which the developer runs agent-written code and confirms that it works, without relying on the agent's own report about tests. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик сам запускает код, написанный агентом, и убеждается, что он работает, не полагаясь на отчёт агента о тестах. [1]

sources.quote: I wrote about this at length last week: the one thing you absolutely cannot outsource to the machine is testing that the code actually works.

definition.en: The practice in which tests are written first and shown to fail, and the agent then writes the implementation until they pass. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой сначала пишут тесты и убеждаются, что они падают, а затем агент пишет реализацию, пока они не пройдут. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: - **Test-driven when possible** - Never disable tests, fix them

sources.quote: Pipe the error in with cat error.log | claude and ask Claude to write a failing test that reproduces the bug. Only after that test goes red do you ask for a fix.
sources.author: Arpan Patel

definition.en: The practice in which the agent reviews its own code before a person reviews it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент делает ревью собственного кода до ревью человеком. [1][2]

sources.quote: Asking the agent to perform a code review on its own work is surprisingly fruitful.
sources.author: Chris Dzombak

sources.quote: My most common one is code review: I tell pi to spawn itself with a code review prompt (via a custom slash command) and it gets the outputs.
sources.author: Mario Zechner

definition.en: The practice in which the developer reads the code an agent wrote before accepting it. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик читает код, написанный агентом, до того как его принять. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: It’s important for me to call out that I believe I’m ultimately responsible for the code that goes into a PR with my name on it, regardless of how it was produced. Therefore, especially in any professional context, I manually review all AI-written code and test cases.
sources.author: Chris Dzombak

sources.quote: I'm not shipping code I don't understand.
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

sources.quote: Please don't ever ship AI-written code without a thorough manual review.
sources.author: Mitchell Hashimoto

definition.en: The practice in which the developer asks the agent to rework the code as many times as it takes to reach an acceptable result. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик просит агента переделывать код столько раз, сколько нужно для приемлемого результата. [1]

sources.quote: If I don’t like what an LLM has written, they’ll never complain at being told to refactor it!
sources.author: Simon Willison

definition.en: The practice in which the developer reviews the changes in a diff view and types corrections into the diff before committing. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик просматривает изменения в диффе и вносит исправления прямо в нём до коммита. [1][2]

sources.quote: The cheapest place to catch a problem is in the diff, before the door closes.
sources.author: Justin Paul

definition.ru: Принцип проектирования: простая система надёжнее сложной. [1]
definition.en: A design principle: a simple system is more reliable than a complex one. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Kelly Johnson, Lockheed, around 1960

sources.quote: Develop simple code that assembles small components into a logical whole, write good documentation, and automate common tasks using standard tools.
sources.author: Erick

origin.en: Attributed to aircraft engineer Kelly Johnson (Lockheed)

definition.ru: Модель разработки, где этапы идут строго по очереди: требования, проектирование, код, тестирование, внедрение. [1]
definition.en: A development model where stages run strictly in order: requirements, design, code, testing, deployment. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Winston Royce, Managing the Development of Large Software Systems, 1970; the word waterfall came later

sources.quote: Specifications aren’t up-front designs because you don’t need to, and probably shouldn’t, develop the entire specification upfront.
sources.author: Marc Brooker

definition.ru: Практика частого слияния изменений в общую ветку с автоматической сборкой и тестами на каждое слияние. [1][2]
definition.en: Merging changes into the shared branch often, with an automatic build and tests on every merge. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Grady Booch, Object-Oriented Design, 1991

sources.quote: The repository operates with minimal blocking merge gates. Pull requests are short-lived.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

sources.quote: With lot of agents working in one repo, build pipelines suffered. To deal with this we introduced a discipline: our agents were to continually commit and rebase from main.
sources.author: Giles Edwards-Alexander

origin.ru: Термин встречается у Грэди Буча, распространился через XP
origin.en: The term appears in Grady Booch's work and spread through XP

definition.ru: Гибкая методология: парное программирование, тесты до кода, непрерывная интеграция, частые релизы. [1]
definition.en: An agile method: pair programming, tests before code, continuous integration, frequent releases. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Kent Beck, Extreme Programming Explained, 1999

sources.quote: TDDing with coding agents keeps them on track, a failing test allows the bots to loop until it finds a working solution to a small increment of behaviour.
sources.author: Benji Weber

origin.ru: Описана Кентом Беком в книге «Extreme Programming Explained»
origin.en: Described by Kent Beck in Extreme Programming Explained

definition.ru: Практика, при которой двое работают над одним кодом: один пишет, другой следит и думает наперёд. [1][2]
definition.en: Two people work on the same code: one types, the other watches and thinks ahead. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Popularised by Extreme Programming, late 1990s

sources.quote: Pairing with coding agents you can spot where they’re working towards the wrong goal and steer them back.
sources.author: Benji Weber

sources.quote: In my experience, you don’t really take turns anymore when you “pair” with an LLM. In the driver-navigator dynamic, you’re spending a lot more time reading the map.
sources.author: Matt Wynne

origin.ru: Стало известно как часть экстремального программирования
origin.en: Became known as part of Extreme Programming

definition.ru: Поиск ошибки через построчное объяснение кода вслух кому угодно, хоть резиновой уточке. [1]
definition.en: Finding a bug by explaining the code line by line out loud to anyone, even a rubber duck. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Andrew Hunt and David Thomas, The Pragmatic Programmer, Oct 1999

sources.quote: I’ve been doing the same thing with AI, just thinking out loud to something that happens to talk back.
sources.author: Emma Klint

origin.ru: Описан Эндрю Хантом и Дэвидом Томасом в книге «Программист-прагматик»
origin.en: Described by Andrew Hunt and David Thomas in The Pragmatic Programmer

definition.ru: Короткое описание требования от лица пользователя: кто, что хочет и зачем. [1]
definition.en: A short requirement written from the user's side: who, what they want, and why. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Extreme Programming, late 1990s

sources.quote: User stories have three critical aspects. We can call these Card, Conversation, and Confirmation.
sources.author: Ron Jeffries

definition.ru: Подход к разработке короткими итерациями с частой обратной связью вместо подробного плана наперёд. [1]
definition.en: Developing in short iterations with frequent feedback instead of a detailed upfront plan. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Manifesto for Agile Software Development, Snowbird, Feb 2001

sources.quote: Engineering speed and throughput is different now, so the way we plan sprints has changed.
sources.author: Claude Code team director (page event summary names Fiona Fung)

origin.ru: Закреплён в Манифесте гибкой разработки, подписанном в Сноуберде
origin.en: Set out in the Agile Manifesto, signed at Snowbird

definition.ru: Практика, при которой сначала пишется падающий тест, затем минимальный код, чтобы он прошёл, затем рефакторинг. [1]
definition.en: Write a failing test first, then the minimal code to pass it, then refactor. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Kent Beck, Test-Driven Development: By Example, 2002; test-first was already part of XP in 1999

sources.quote: When working on a new feature or a bug fix, you always write a failing test or series of tests first and then wait for me to review them.
sources.author: thoughtbot (author name not shown in the saved text)

origin.ru: Сформулирована Кентом Беком в книге «Test-Driven Development: By Example»
origin.en: Formulated by Kent Beck in Test-Driven Development: By Example

definition.ru: Отдельная ветка в системе контроля версий на каждую фичу, которая сливается в основную после готовности. [1]
definition.en: A separate version-control branch per feature, merged into the main branch when ready. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Approximate: Git released Apr 2005; the practice is older

sources.quote: A feature branch is a source code branching pattern where a developer opens a branch when she starts working on a new feature.
sources.author: Martin Fowler

origin.ru: Стала нормой вместе с Git и GitHub
origin.en: Became the norm with Git and GitHub

definition.ru: Запрос на слияние изменений, вокруг которого идут обсуждение и ревью. [1][2]
definition.en: A request to merge changes that hosts the discussion and review. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: GitHub, 2008

sources.quote: Reviewing your own pull request isn’t optional when agents are involved.
sources.author: GitHub Blog (author name not shown in the saved text)

sources.quote: Because Copilot starts looking at comments as soon as they are submitted, if you are likely to make multiple comments on a pull request it's best to batch them by clicking Start a review, rather than clicking Add single comment.
sources.author: GitHub

definition.en: An approach in which software is produced the way industry produces goods, with standard tools and a managed process. [1]
definition.ru: Подход, при котором софт производят так, как промышленность производит товары: со стандартными инструментами и управляемым процессом. [1]

firstAppeared.note: Year stated by Addy Osmani (2026): Bob Bemer, «The economics of program production», 1968

sources.quote: This idea of the software factory is a term that dates back to Bob Bemer’s paper, “The economics of program production,” given in 1968.
sources.author: Addy Osmani

origin.en: Proposed by Bob Bemer in «The economics of program production»
origin.ru: Предложил Боб Бемер в докладе «The economics of program production»

definition.en: The practice in which a large mechanical change across a codebase is made by a program that rewrites the code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой большую механическую правку по всей кодовой базе делает программа, переписывающая код. [1]

sources.quote: A codemod is a program that operates on a codebase, and when you give an AI agent the ability to write and execute them, these platform-level tasks fall below the high-water mark of AI capabilities.
sources.author: Codegen Technical Staff

definition.en: The practice in which a team spends a small, fixed number of «innovation tokens» on new technologies and uses well-known ones for everything else. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда тратит небольшое фиксированное число «жетонов на новизну» на новые технологии, а в остальном берёт хорошо известные. [1][2]

firstAppeared.note: Dan McKinley, «Choose Boring Technology», dated on the page

sources.quote: Let’s say every company gets about three innovation tokens.
sources.author: Dan McKinley

sources.quote: I thought coding agents would prove to be the ultimate embodiment of the Choose Boring Technology approach, but in practice they don’t seem to be affecting my technology choices in that way at all.
sources.author: Simon Willison

origin.en: Set out by Dan McKinley in «Choose Boring Technology»
origin.ru: Изложил Дэн Маккинли в посте «Choose Boring Technology»

definition.en: An approach to manufacturing in which a factory runs without people on site, so it can work with the lights off. [1]
definition.ru: Подход к производству, при котором завод работает без людей на месте и может работать с выключенным светом. [1]

sources.quote: An AI dark factory applies the same idea to software: a defined class of development work running autonomously through implementation, verification, and delivery, with humans defining goals and constraints, setting the process, and handling exceptions rather than supervising every step.
sources.author: Owen Sweeney

definition.en: The practice in which a screen layout is sketched roughly, without visual detail, before the interface is designed or built. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой раскладку экрана набрасывают грубо, без визуальных деталей, до того как интерфейс проектируют или делают. [1]

sources.quote: Prototyping has come full circle. From Balsamiq’s intentional sketchiness → to Figma’s pixel-perfect fidelity → to ASCII’s structured minimalism.
sources.author: Carlos Chinchilla

title.ru: Document & Clear (план в файл и сброс)

definition.en: The practice in which, for a large task, the agent writes its plan and progress to a file, the context is cleared, and a new session reads the file and continues the work. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой на большой задаче агент записывает план и ход работы в файл, контекст очищается, а новая сессия читает этот файл и продолжает работу. [1][2]

sources.quote: For large tasks. I have Claude dump its plan and progress into a .md, /clear the state, then start a new session by telling it to read the .md and continue.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

sources.quote: If you need task tracking, make it externally stateful by writing to a file:
sources.author: Mario Zechner

definition.en: The practice in which a team records its code rules in the repository and on a regular cadence runs background agent tasks that look for deviations from the rules or stale documentation and open pull requests with fixes. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда записывает правила кода в репозиторий и регулярно запускает фоновые задачи агента, которые ищут отступления от правил или устаревшую документацию и открывают pull request с исправлениями. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: Instead, we started encoding what we call “golden principles” directly into the repository and built a recurring cleanup process.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

sources.quote: Suppose you want Claude to handle a task automatically on a recurring basis, like reviewing open PRs every morning, auditing dependencies weekly, or checking for CI failures overnight.
sources.author: Anthropic

sources.quote: If there’s a check you already run every morning by hand, that’s your first loop.
sources.author: Addy Osmani

definition.en: The practice in which saved agent session logs are reviewed regularly, by scripts, people or another agent, for repeated errors and permission requests, and the agent's instructions and tools are changed in response. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой сохранённые логи сессий агента регулярно разбирают скриптами, людьми или другим агентом в поисках повторяющихся ошибок и запросов разрешений, и по итогам меняют инструкции и инструменты агента. [1][2]

sources.quote: I have scripts that run meta-analysis on these logs, looking for common exceptions, permission requests, and error patterns to help improve agent-facing context.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

sources.quote: Use scheduled tasks for reflection and maintenance, not just execution.
sources.author: OpenAI

title.en: Agent review of every pull request

definition.en: The practice in which a team has an agent review every pull request, and review by a person becomes optional. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда отдаёт каждый pull request на ревью агенту, а ревью человеком становится необязательным. [1][2]

sources.quote: Humans may review pull requests, but aren’t required to. Over time, we’ve pushed almost all review effort towards being handled agent-to-agent.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

sources.quote: At OpenAI, Codex reviews 100% of PRs.
sources.author: OpenAI

definition.en: The practice in which an agent drives a browser on the running application to check a change against each acceptance criterion and reports what it saw, with screenshots, for each criterion. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент управляет браузером на запущенном приложении, проверяет изменение по каждому критерию приёмки и сообщает по каждому критерию, что увидел, со скриншотами. [1]

sources.quote: Once the agent builds the feature, verification runs Playwright browser agents against each AC, takes screenshots, and produces a report with per-criterion verdicts.
sources.author: Abhishek Ray

definition.en: The practice in which the agent runs with broad permissions, up to root, on a throwaway machine or virtual machine that has no access to production systems or secrets beyond what development needs. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент работает с широкими правами, вплоть до root, на одноразовой машине или виртуальной машине без доступа к продакшену и без секретов сверх нужных для разработки. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: I run Claude Code in permissive mode. The VM is isolated—no access to production systems, no secrets beyond what’s needed for development.
sources.author: Granda

sources.quote: I built a thing called the observatory (very very earlier) that will run firecracker VMs that have a network ingress/egress shims, and file I/O shims so that I can audit and watch what the agents are doing.
sources.author: Harper Reed

sources.quote: I have tried just about everything and I highly recommend: use a fresh VM.
sources.author: crawshaw

definition.en: The practice in which services are given to the agent as small command-line tools, each with a README that the agent reads only when it needs the tool, instead of MCP servers. [1][2][3][4]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой сервисы отдают агенту как небольшие утилиты командной строки, у каждой свой README, который агент читает только когда утилита нужна, вместо MCP-серверов. [1][2][3][4]

sources.quote: All my stateless tools (like Jira, AWS, GitHub) have been migrated to simple CLIs.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

sources.quote: The alternative is simple: build CLI tools with README files. The agent reads the README when it needs the tool, pays the token cost only when necessary (progressive disclosure), and can use bash to invoke the tool.
sources.author: Mario Zechner

sources.quote: One of the reasons we strongly lean towards CLI and bash is because it allows easy composition of calls, and because the model also learns how the file system works when it’s trained.
sources.author: Armin Ronacher

sources.quote: The simplest form is text, so by default, whatever I wanna build, it starts as CLI. Agents can call it directly and verify output - closing the loop.
sources.author: Peter Steinberger

definition.en: The practice in which a team runs the same agent tasks as evals with and without a change to instruction files or documentation, and keeps the change only after several runs show an improvement. [1][2][3]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда прогоняет одни и те же задачи агента как evals с изменением в файлах инструкций или документации и без него и оставляет изменение, только если несколько прогонов показали улучшение. [1][2][3]

sources.quote: Build evals targeting APIs not in training data. That's where doc access matters most.
sources.author: Jude Gao

sources.quote: To test these concerns, we created a set of evaluations that measured agent performance within our current setup against a branch without root-level documentation files.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda

sources.quote: Only try to complete this task using the raw model and harness. And see, is it actually okay without using any of these skills?
sources.author: Addy Osmani

title.en: Check that the instruction file is loaded

definition.en: The practice in which the developer checks which instruction file the agent tool actually reads, for example with a marker word, before relying on it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик проверяет, какой файл инструкций агент на самом деле читает, например по контрольному слову, прежде чем на него полагаться. [1][2]

sources.quote: Check which filename your harness actually honours, because an ignored instruction file is silent.
sources.author: Systima

sources.quote: I made an empty directory that holds only an AGENTS.md with a canary word in it, and asked claude -p for the word.
sources.author: Przemek

definition.en: The practice in which a prompt or workflow that the developer keeps repeating is saved as a skill or command file, checked into git and run by name. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой промпт или порядок действий, который разработчик повторяет снова и снова, сохраняется как скилл или команда, кладётся в git и запускается по имени. [1][2]

sources.quote: But I was able to coach it, and once it was in a good place I had it make a skill based on what we discovered together.
sources.author: Harper Reed

sources.quote: If you do something more than once a day, turn it into a skill. Anything you repeat is a skill waiting to be written.
sources.author: Arpan Patel

title.en: Repository knowledge as the system of record

definition.en: The practice in which decisions, plans, conventions and other context are kept as versioned files in the repository instead of chats, documents and people's heads, so that agents can read them. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой решения, планы, соглашения и прочий контекст хранятся как версионируемые файлы в репозитории, а не в чатах, документах и головах людей, чтобы агенты могли их прочитать. [1][2]

sources.quote: We learned that we needed to push more and more context into the repo over time.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

sources.quote: PRDs, ADRs, UI Specs, and Design Docs live in their own directories (docs/prd/, docs/adr/, docs/ui-spec/, docs/design/) and are intended to be committed.
sources.author: shinpr

definition.en: The practice in which a long agent session is summarized at a milestone or near the context limit, with instructions on what the summary keeps, and work continues in a new context from the summary. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой длинную сессию агента сжимают в краткое изложение на рубеже работы или у предела контекста, с указанием, что сохранить, и работа продолжается в новом контексте с этого изложения. [1]

sources.quote: Compact at milestones. After you finish a logical chunk, run /compact Preserve the decisions made, files changed, and test commands.
sources.author: Arpan Patel

definition.en: The practice in which several agents or models work on the same problem at the same time, each with its own approach, and the developer compares the results. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой несколько агентов или моделей одновременно работают над одной задачей, каждый своим подходом, а разработчик сравнивает результаты. [1][2]

sources.quote: Another researcher explained that they ran many versions of Claude simultaneously, all exploring different approaches to a problem:
sources.author: Saffron Huang, Bryan Seethor, Esin Durmus, Kunal Handa, Miles McCain, Michael Stern, Deep Ganguli

sources.quote: We've found that having multiple models attempt the same problem and picking the best result significantly improves the final output, especially for harder tasks.
sources.author: Lee Robinson

definition.en: The practice in which the application can be started separately in each git worktree, so that every agent runs and checks its own instance. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой приложение запускается отдельно в каждом git worktree, и каждый агент запускает и проверяет свой экземпляр. [1]

sources.quote: For example, we made the app bootable per git worktree, so Codex could launch and drive one instance per change.
sources.author: Ryan Lopopolo

title.en: Vulnerability hunting agents with test proof
title.ru: Поиск уязвимостей агентами с доказательством тестом

definition.en: The practice in which agents search parts of an application for one category of vulnerability, a separate verifier agent proves each finding with a test in the application's own test suite, and findings arrive as pull requests. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенты ищут в частях приложения уязвимости одной категории, отдельный агент-проверяющий доказывает каждую находку тестом в наборе тестов самого приложения, а находки приходят как pull request. [1]

sources.quote: Our Verifier agent is tasked with authoring and embedding its validations into the existing tests and primitives available in that app.
sources.author: Zack Deveau

title.en: Vertical slices in agent work plans

definition.en: The practice in which the agent's work plan for a feature is cut into vertical slices that cross backend and frontend, so that integration is exercised before the end of the work. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой план работы агента над фичей режут на вертикальные срезы через бэкенд и фронтенд, чтобы интеграция проверялась до конца работы. [1]

sources.quote: Backend and frontend design stay separate, a consistency check covers the boundary between them, and the work plan uses vertical slices so integration is exercised before the end.
sources.author: shinpr

definition.en: The practice in which contributors state in the pull request, commit message or post whether and how a model or agent produced the content. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой участники указывают в pull request, коммите или сообщении, создавали ли содержимое модель или агент и как. [1][2]

sources.quote: Contributors should note tool usage in their pull request description, commit message, or wherever authorship is normally indicated for the work.
sources.author: rnk

sources.quote: You must disclose LLM-generated content. You can choose to not post LLM content, or you can choose to post it and disclose its origin.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson

definition.en: The practice in which a project requires contributors to read and review all generated code or text, and to be able to explain it, before they ask maintainers for review. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект требует от авторов вкладов прочитать и проверить весь сгенерированный код или текст и уметь его объяснить, прежде чем просить ревью у мейнтейнеров. [1][2]

sources.quote: Contributors must read and review all LLM-generated code or text before they ask other project members to review it.
sources.author: rnk

sources.quote: LLM reviews cannot substitute for human review or self-review.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson

title.ru: Свои слова в общении в проекте

definition.en: The practice in which a project requires issues, pull request descriptions, comments and replies to review to be written in the contributor's own words, not pasted model output. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект требует, чтобы issues, описания pull request, комментарии и ответы на ревью были написаны своими словами автора, а не вставленным выводом модели. [1][2]

sources.quote: Passing maintainer feedback to an LLM doesn’t help anyone grow, and does not sustain our community.
sources.author: rnk

sources.quote: In short, if you are posting any of those things, the output must be your own words, explanation, description, etc., not a verbatim dump of an LLM's output.
sources.author: Jellyfin project

title.en: Agents in project spaces only with approval
title.ru: Агенты в пространствах проекта только с одобрения

definition.en: The practice in which an agent may comment on or act in shared project spaces only after people approve it or explicitly invoke it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агент может комментировать или действовать в общих пространствах проекта только после одобрения людьми или по явному вызову. [1][2]

sources.quote: An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub @claude agent.
sources.author: rnk

sources.quote: This skill requires explicit invocation because it can comment, label, or close another person's contribution.
sources.author: Wirasm

definition.en: The practice in which maintainers who judge a generated contribution to cost more review time than it is worth reply with a standard request, label it, and stop engaging or close it. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой мейнтейнеры, решив, что сгенерированный вклад отнимает на ревью больше времени, чем стоит, отвечают стандартной просьбой, ставят метку и прекращают обсуждение или закрывают вклад. [1][2]

sources.quote: Other reviewers should use the label to prioritize their review time.
sources.author: rnk

sources.quote: You are allowed to close PRs that don't follow the policy, no questions asked. Please point the author to #llm-mentoring at the same time.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson

definition.en: The practice in which a project does not accept contributions that include content generated, in part or in full, by language models or similar systems. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект не принимает вклады, содержащие материал, созданный целиком или частично языковыми моделями или похожими системами. [1]

sources.quote: Contributions in the OpenJDK Community must not include content generated, in part or in full, by large language models, diffusion models, or similar deep-learning systems.
sources.author: OpenJDK Governing Board

definition.en: The practice in which a project lets contributors use language models to answer questions, analyze, check and review their work, but not to create the content they submit. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект разрешает участникам использовать языковые модели, чтобы отвечать на вопросы, анализировать, проверять и ревьюить свою работу, но не создавать то, что они присылают. [1]

sources.quote: LLMs must not generate soundness-critical changes unless the author is already a domain expert, and even then it's strongly discouraged.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson

definition.en: The practice in which shared agent controls used by many teams, such as skills, commands and root-level instruction files, have an owning team or guild that watches monitoring data and updates them. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой у общих настроек агентов для многих команд, таких как скиллы, команды и корневые файлы инструкций, есть команда или гильдия-владелец, которая следит за данными мониторинга и обновляет их. [1]

sources.quote: On the other hand, more complex controls like skills, commands, or root-level documentation may be owned by entire teams or guilds.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda

title.ru: Вопросы об агентах в разборе инцидентов

definition.en: The practice in which a team's regular incident retrospective adds two questions: whether agent-written code contributed to the incident, and whether the larger volume of change strained review, testing, rollout or observability. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой в регулярный разбор инцидентов команды добавляют два вопроса: повлиял ли на инцидент код, написанный агентом, и не перегрузил ли возросший объём изменений ревью, тестирование, выкатку или наблюдаемость. [1]

sources.quote: During our AI ramp-up, we began asking two additional questions: Did AI-authored code directly contribute to the incident? And did the increased volume of change put additional pressure on review, testing, rollout, or observability?
sources.author: Tyson Singer

title.en: Extra approval for agent pull requests
title.ru: Повышенная планка для pull request агента

definition.en: The practice in which pull requests started by an agent or generated by a model must clear a higher bar than other pull requests, such as more human approvals or required tests. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой pull request, начатые агентом или созданные моделью, должны пройти более высокую планку, чем остальные: больше одобрений людей или обязательные тесты. [1][2]

sources.quote: We’ve settled on 2 human approvals for any AI-initiated PR for now, but it is kind of a weird paradigm shift (for me at least) when it’s no longer a human making something for another human to review.
sources.author: Shrivu Shankar

sources.quote: LLM PRs are required to have tests, full stop, regardless of how hard that is, as well as various other restrictions;
sources.author: Jynn Nelson

definition.en: The practice in which an engineer now and then solves a problem without an agent, even one the agent could solve, to keep their own skills. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой инженер время от времени решает задачу без агента, даже если агент бы с ней справился, чтобы сохранить свои навыки. [1]

sources.quote: To combat this, some engineers deliberately practice without AI: "Every once in a while, even if I know that Claude can nail a problem, I will not ask it to. It helps me keep myself sharp."
sources.author: Saffron Huang, Bryan Seethor, Esin Durmus, Kunal Handa, Miles McCain, Michael Stern, Deep Ganguli

definition.en: The practice in which an interview gives the candidate a few hours to build a working prototype with coding agents and tools of their choice. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой на собеседовании кандидату дают несколько часов, чтобы собрать работающий прототип с агентами и инструментами на свой выбор. [1][2]

sources.quote: After that, the candidate gets two hours to build a working prototype of the system they just designed using any AI model they want, and any frameworks.
sources.author: Applied Intuition

sources.quote: The centerpiece of our on-site was a three-hour build session. Candidates chose from a short list of assigned prompts and were asked to design, build, and deploy a working prototype on DigitalOcean by the end of the session.
sources.author: DigitalOcean

title.en: Assessing how a candidate directs agents
title.ru: Оценка того, как кандидат направляет агента

definition.en: The practice in which interviewers score how a candidate plans the work, steers the agent and checks what it produced. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой интервьюеры оценивают, как кандидат планирует работу, направляет агента и проверяет результат. [1][2]

sources.quote: Steering, not just prompting. Are you thinking about the how and why of the work, or just feeding the spec to an agent and hoping for the best?
sources.author: Elicit

sources.quote: Can they effectively direct and validate AI-generated work?
sources.author: Augment Code

title.en: Candidate's own agents in the interview

definition.en: The practice in which a candidate may use their own coding agents and tools during an interview, the same ones they would use at work. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой кандидат может пользоваться на собеседовании своими агентами и инструментами, теми же, что и на работе. [1][2]

sources.quote: The interviews where we want you to use AI tend to be deeper technical sessions. You’re on your own machine, using whatever tools you’re comfortable with.
sources.author: Elicit

sources.quote: We’re open to any type of tools, from none at all, to autocompletes, to full coding agents.
sources.author: Omnea

title.en: Review of a draft change in the interview

definition.en: The practice in which a candidate reviews and improves a colleague's draft pull request in an unfamiliar codebase, with agents allowed. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой кандидат на собеседовании проверяет и дорабатывает черновой pull request коллеги в незнакомой кодовой базе, с агентами. [1]

sources.quote: Candidates are given a medium-sized codebase and a draft PR from a colleague that introduces a cross-cutting feature. Their job is to review and improve it — pulling down the code, inspecting the output, and iterating with coding agents to make it better.
sources.author: Sierra

definition.en: The practice in which some interviews are deliberately held without agents, next to interviews where agents are expected. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой часть собеседований намеренно проводят без агентов, рядом с теми, где агенты ожидаются. [1]

sources.quote: There are some interviews where we explicitly ask candidates not to use AI.
sources.author: Elicit

title.en: Regular audit of the agent setup

definition.en: The practice in which, every few weeks, the developer audits the agent setup, including skills, plugins, instruction files and memory, with the tool's check command and reviews which parts still hold true. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой разработчик раз в несколько недель проверяет настройку агента, включая скиллы, плагины, файлы инструкций и память, командой проверки инструмента и пересматривает, что из этого ещё верно. [1]

sources.quote: And so I think there’s high value personally in, like maybe every couple of weeks, maybe at once a month even, just running doctor on your skills, on your setup, and auditing what you’re doing and seeing, okay, well, what still holds true?
sources.author: Addy Osmani

definition.en: The practice in which tests are kept as data files with the input, the expected output and the setup, read by a small test runner, so that agent changes to the tests are visible and can be blocked. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой тесты хранятся как файлы данных со входом, ожидаемым результатом и подготовкой, а читает их небольшой тестовый раннер, чтобы правки агента в тестах были видны и их можно было запретить. [1]

sources.quote: The tests are a contract that establishes what the code should do for us, and moving tests to data files, interpreted by a relatively smaller test runner, makes them easier to protect from unexpected manipulation by AI.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari

definition.en: The practice in which faults are injected into production code, by hand, by the agent or by a library in CI, to check that tests written by an agent break with a clear error message. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой в продакшен-код вносят намеренные ошибки, вручную, руками агента или библиотекой в CI, и проверяют, что тесты, написанные агентом, падают с понятным сообщением об ошибке. [1]

sources.quote: The first thing we can do is mutation testing: we inject intentional faults in production code, and see if any test breaks, and if it breaks, check that the error message is correct and informative.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari

definition.en: The practice in which test files and expected results that a task should not change are protected from the agent: made read-only, checked in CI for changes, or named in the agent's instructions as inputs to keep. [1][2]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой файлы тестов и ожидаемые результаты, которые задача не должна менять, защищают от агента: делают доступными только для чтения, проверяют на изменения в CI или указывают в инструкциях агента как неизменяемые. [1][2]

sources.quote: Depending on the type of task, it’s possible to protect the files that we’re not expecting the AI to change, by making them read-only in a way that the agent cannot bypass, or by running a check in CI that verifies what files were changed depending on the type of task.
sources.author: Matteo Vaccari

sources.quote: The agent was instructed to preserve those inputs and the skill’s verification helpers, investigate failures, and correct the implementation or execution setup rather than weaken the expectations.
sources.author: Naresh Jain

definition.en: The practice in which, for medium- and high-risk pull requests, an agent guides the engineer through how the change affects the system, with understanding of the change, not approval, as the goal. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой для pull request среднего и высокого риска агент проводит инженера по тому, как изменение влияет на систему, и цель — понимание изменения, а не одобрение. [1]

sources.quote: We’ve been experimenting with a new process called Intent Review. For medium and high risk PRs, the agent guides the engineer through understanding how the change affects the system.
sources.author: Vinay Perneti and Emma Webb

definition.en: The practice in which agents read the codebase, issues, pull requests and discussion threads and write a knowledge base of unrecorded decisions and conventions, which other agents use when they work on the code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой агенты читают код, issues, pull request и обсуждения и пишут базу знаний о незаписанных решениях и соглашениях, которой другие агенты пользуются, когда работают с кодом. [1]

sources.quote: Agents that crawl the codebase, the issues, the PRs, the threads, and produce a knowledge base of the implicit decisions, the conventions, the why-we-did-it-this-way that nobody had time to document.
sources.author: .txt

title.ru: Управление агентом на самом узком уровне

definition.en: The practice in which a team corrects an agent behavior with the control of the smallest scope that still gives the wanted output: first interface and output contracts, then automated checks, then skills or commands, and root instruction files last. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой команда исправляет поведение агента средством самого узкого охвата, которое ещё даёт нужный результат: сначала контракты интерфейса и вывода, затем автоматические проверки, затем скиллы или команды и в последнюю очередь корневые файлы инструкций. [1]

sources.quote: At Datadog, we aim to use the control with the smallest scope that still gives us the output we want.
sources.author: Addie Beach, Rui Martins Lacerda

title.en: Volunteer-only review of model-written pull requests
title.ru: Ревью pull request от модели только добровольцами

definition.en: The practice in which a project assigns pull requests written with a language model only to reviewers who volunteer for them, and such a reviewer may ask the author to redo the change without generated code. [1]
definition.ru: Практика, при которой проект отдаёт pull request, написанные с помощью языковой модели, только тем ревьюерам, кто вызвался их проверять, и такой ревьюер может попросить автора переделать изменение без сгенерированного кода. [1]

sources.quote: No one is required to review LLM PRs unless they volunteer.
sources.author: Jynn Nelson
